speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe the nature of your diarrhea and how long you have been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any weight loss, fever, or blood in your stool, and have you noticed any changes in your skin or joints? REQUEST TEST: Stool_Ova_and_Parasites

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal parasitic screen and your symptoms of mucus, urgency, and pain relief with defecation, I suspect an inflammatory or functional bowel disorder. REQUEST TEST: Colonoscopy_with_Biopsy

speaker: Doctor
text: Since structural and infectious causes have been ruled out, do you experience symptom worsening during times of stress or with certain food triggers? I also need to know if you have ever been diagnosed with anxiety, depression, or irritable bowel syndrome in the past.

speaker: Doctor
text: It seems the patient's response was garbled, but given the normal colonoscopy and stool tests, your symptoms strongly point to Irritable Bowel Syndrome. I would like to check for any underlying celiac disease or lactose intolerance that might be contributing to your discomfort. REQUEST TEST: Celiac_Serology_and_Lactose_Hydrogen_Breath_Test

speaker: Doctor
text: With celiac disease and lactose intolerance ruled out, I need to determine if your symptoms are purely functional or if there is a microscopic inflammation. Do you experience any bloating or abdominal distension, and have you noticed any correlation between your symptoms and menstrual cycles? REQUEST TEST: Fecal_Calprotectin

speaker: Doctor
text: Your normal fecal calprotectin confirms there is no significant intestinal inflammation, ruling out inflammatory bowel disease. Given your chronic symptoms of abdominal pain relieved by defecation, urgency, and mucus in the stool without any organic cause, I am ready to diagnose you. DIAGNOSIS READY: Irritable Bowel Syndrome
